newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition puts united face forward in crisis.
newsitem.headline: India coalition puts united face forward in crisis.

text.p: Leaders of India's ruling coalition, defiant in a political crisis, said on Thursday that attempts by the Congress party to divide their ranks and ride to power would not succeed.

A day before facing a vote of confidence in parliament after the withdrawal of vital support by the Congress, the 15-party United Front's decision-making Steering Committee snubbed the Congress's persistent demand for a change in leadership.
"Whatever happens, we will face parliament," Harkishan Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) told a crowded news conference.

Earlier, leaders of the coalition that groups communists, free-marketers and regional parties, had a meeting after the Congress demanded that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda step down before 11 a.m.(0530 GMT) on Friday or face a hostile vote.
"The United Front is united. Nobody can do anything (to divide us)," said Chandrababu Naidu, chief minister of the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, who leads the regional Telugu Desam Party.
Surjeet said there was no question of Deve Gowda quitting the leadership, because the front was concerned with issues, not personalities.

On March 30, Congress president Sitaram Kesri withdrew support to the 10-month-old coalition, formed last year to oust a 12-day-old government formed by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) parliament's single largest group.
Kesri, who later staked a claim to form a Congress-led coalition, accused Deve Gowda of not combating "communal forces," a reference to the BJP.

Surjeet said in two days of formal talks, the Congress refused to accept suggestions from the ruling front for the establishment of a coordination committee to address complaints, and instead harped on removing Deve Gowda.
"We told them the objective seems to be to present the United Front as unreasonable," Surjeet said.
The coalition, accused by the Congress of not closing ranks to fight the BJP, aimed to turn the tables on the group.
"They can't bring down the government without the support of the BJP," Surjeet said. "Let us see if they join hands with the people whom we opposed (together)," he said.
"We have decided to go to parliament, place our decision and defend it," he said. "It is for the people and parliament to judge."
The United Front has 178 lawmakers in the 545-member parliament, and is support by a handful of splinter groups. The Congress has 140 members and the BJP and its allies 193.
